newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks end mixed, Zagrebacka recovers.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks end mixed, Zagrebacka recovers.

text.p: Croatian stocks closed mixed on Friday in livelier trade, with Zagrebacka Banka partly recovering from a recent slide.
But traders said Friday was perhaps the last day of relatively active trade on the Zagreb bourse ahead of the summer holidays.
Of 16 active issues seven fell, six rose, two were flat and one traded for the first time this year. Volume doubled to 10,097 units, while turnover tripled to 10.2 million kuna.
"The volume and the prices will probably fall next week," a trader with a large market share said. "This was probably the last active day of the season."
Friday was dominated by Zagrebacka recovering some of the ground it had lost in recent days.
It added 30 kuna to close at 1,950 on the day's record volume of 3,083 shares, following its rise in London where its GDRs, issued ten for each share, added $0.25 to $32 by mid afternoon.
"The price is still relatively low so it could go up in the next few days," the trader said.
Zagrebacka's preferred stock added 15 kuna to 1,495, and traders said there was still room for it to grow, closing the gap with the bank's ordinary share.
The other market heavyweight, drugs firm Pliva, lost four kuna to 470 on volume of 1,417, but traders were optimistic.
"I don't think Pliva could go down any further, as investors are likely to start buying it at this price," the trader said.

Karlovacka Pivovara, the market's darling in recent days, in which it almost doubled in value from 360 two weeks ago to 610 kuna at one point on Thursday, led the decliners. It lost 13 kuna to close at 588, trading only 258 shares.
"Karlovacka rose primarily because of small investors who cannot support it at this price, so its suffered a correction," the trader said, adding that the stock is promising in the long run.
Top gainer hotelier Riviera added eight kuna to 155 on volume of 965 shares. Of four other hotelier stocks one rose, two fell and one was flat.
